title: Decode Ways
description:
A message of letters is encoded as digits using `A = 1, B = 2, ..., Z = 26`. Given a string `s` of digits, return the **number of ways** to decode it.

For example, `"11106"` decodes as `AAJF` (1 1 10 6) or `KJF` (11 10 6). Groups with a leading zero, such as `"06"`, are not valid. If no valid decoding exists, return `0`.
constraints: s contains only digits and may have leading zeros.
hints: ways[i] depends on whether the last one digit and the last two digits form a valid letter.
Only the previous two counts are needed.
